subject: series
synopsis: Brian Buccellato's seven-issue crossover event colliding the DC superheroes with Godzilla, King Kong, and the Monsterverse's roster of kaiju when cosmic technology tears rifts between universes. A gleefully fun concept executed with crowd-pleasing energy — watching Batman try to stop Godzilla is exactly the spectacle the premise promises.
author: Brian Buccellato

subject: series
synopsis: Spin-off series set in the Spawn universe exploring Al Simmons' ongoing war against both Heaven and Hell as he solidifies his role as the reigning king of the underworld.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Wagner's Vertigo series tracing the immortal sorceress Nimue through history. Beautifully illustrated by Amy Reeder Hadley; a rich showcase of DC's magical history.
author: Matt Wagner

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's psychological portrait of Magneto operating alone as a vigilante after breaking with Cyclops, hunting down human persecutors of mutants. Dark, morally complex, and featuring Magneto at his most fearsome.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell's New 52 series is controversial but has genuine character development for Jason Todd. The Scott Lobdell run is polarizing; Lobdell's later run is more consistent.
author: Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: Andy Lanning and Dan Abnett's 1997 series about Mitch Shelley, a man who resurrects with a different power each time he dies, wanted by Heaven, Hell, and the DC universe alike. A clever high-concept series.
author: Andy Lanning, Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: A compendium of J. Michael Straczynski's epic superhero saga about 113 people granted powers by a mysterious prenatal event and the consequences for humanity.
author: J. Michael Straczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Bil Keane's wholesome American newspaper strip, launched in 1960, following the four Keane children — Billy, Dolly, Jeffy, and PJ — through everyday family life. Known for its distinctive circular panel format and its gently observational humor about parenting and childhood, it became one of the most-read strips in newspaper history; Jeff Keane has carried it on since his father's death in 2011.
author: Bil Keane

subject: series
synopsis: Original issues of EC Comics' The Vault of Horror (1950-1955), one of the most celebrated and influential horror anthology comics ever published, featuring gruesome twist-ending tales from some of the finest cartoonists of the era.
author: Bill Gaines / Al Feldstein
artist: Johnny Craig / Jack Davis / Graham Ingels

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Pat Olliffe's 1995 series of new stories set in Spider-Man's early Lee/Ditko years, slotted between the classic issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey's late Wildstorm run reimagined the team as a corporation using alien technology to solve energy problems. Unusual superhero deconstruction with real-world consequence focus.

subject: series
synopsis: DC series introducing Ray Terrill, a young man raised in total darkness who discovers he can transform himself into living light energy — part of a legacy connected to the golden-age hero the Ray. Written initially by Jack C. Harris and later by Christopher Priest, whose run added notable psychological complexity to the character.
author: Jack C. Harris

subject: series
synopsis: Swamp Thing volume 4 (2004-2006): Andy Diggle's opening and Joshua Dysart's run with Tefé Holland, the last Vertigo Swamp Thing.

subject: series
synopsis: The Authority in Wildstorm's post-apocalyptic World's End (2008-2010): the team stranded in a ruined London fused with their Carrier, by Abnett and Lanning.

subject: series
synopsis: Sholly Fisch's 2008 all-ages Super Friends, based on the Imaginext toy line: Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, Flash, Green Lantern and Aquaman in kid-friendly adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: A comic series.

subject: series
synopsis: Marguerite Bennett and Rafael de Latorre's 2016 series: when animals suddenly gain intelligence, the dog Sandor guards a young girl, Jesse, across a violent new America.

subject: series
synopsis: Kazue Kato's manga about the son of Satan raised to be an exorcist. Strong shonen action with a compelling moral core — Rin's refusal to be defined by his origins is effective.
author: Kazue Kato

subject: series
synopsis: Catwoman's New 52 series (2011-2016): Judd Winick and Guillem March's notorious opener, then Ann Nocenti and Genevieve Valentine's Catwoman-as-mob-boss arc.

subject: series
synopsis: The series renaming Daken's book as he operates as a villain under Norman Osborn's reign during Dark Reign, continuing the examination of Wolverine's son as a morally unredeemable but fascinating anti-hero.
author: Daniel Way, Marjorie Liu

subject: series
synopsis: Kei Sasuga's romance manga about a high school student who discovers that the woman he slept with and his teacher crush are stepsisters who move into his house. Melodramatic and unapologetically pulpy; finds genuine emotional complexity in an outrageous premise.
author: Kei Sasuga

subject: series
synopsis: Milestone's alien superhero who landed in antebellum America and has lived as a conservative Black man. Dwayne McDuffie's political complexity makes this one of the most interesting superhero concepts ever.
author: Dwayne McDuffie

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen's Krakoa-era series following the Quiet Council of Krakoa from the perspective of Hope and other council members, applying Gillen's political and psychological acuity to mutant governance.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: Noelle Stevenson, Shannon Watters, and Grace Ellis's Boom Studios series about a group of girls at a supernatural summer camp became a cultural phenomenon for its inclusive cast, warm friendships, and joyful monster-fighting adventures. One of the most acclaimed all-ages comics of the decade, earning multiple Eisner Awards and cementing Boom's reputation for progressive, diverse storytelling.
author: Noelle Stevenson, Shannon Watters, Grace Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter's landmark 1984 crossover event transplanting Marvel's heroes and villains to a 'Battleworld' built by the godlike Beyonder. The first modern comic book crossover event; introduced the black Spider-Man symbiote costume. A landmark despite its rushed production.
author: Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Bedard's CrossGen series following a diverse ensemble of sigil-bearers from across the CrossGen universe who are captured and imprisoned by Charon, the tyrannical ruler of the Negation — an anti-matter dimension opposed to all life. Praised for its large, well-managed cast and propulsive action across its 27-issue run.
author: Tony Bedard

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's weekly anthology magazine published 1992–1993, featuring serialized strips starring various Marvel UK characters — Death's Head II, Motormouth, Killpower, Dark Angel, and others. Part of Marvel UK's ambitious early 1990s attempt to build a distinct superhero universe separate from the American Marvel line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Nobuhiro Watsuki's beloved historical action manga follows Kenshin Himura, a legendary assassin of the Meiji Revolution who has sworn never to kill again. The Kyoto arc in particular is considered one of shonen manga's finest story arcs.
author: Nobuhiro Watsuki

subject: series
synopsis: IPC's short-lived 1978 sister weekly to 2000 AD, which introduced Strontium Dog and Ro-Busters before merging into 2000 AD.

subject: series
synopsis: Jamie Hewlett and Alan Martin's anarchic post-apocalyptic Tank Girl in her definitive classic form — a foul-mouthed punk mercenary living in her tank in a destroyed Australia, drawn with Hewlett's extraordinary visual energy.
author: Alan Martin

subject: series
synopsis: Comedy tie-in to the animated series. Pure all-ages fun that embraces the show's absurdist energy. Not trying to be anything other than what it is — and executes that very well.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: EC's 1950-1954 horror anthology hosted by the Old Witch, with Graham Ingels' ghoulish art and Gaines and Feldstein's twist-ending tales.
author: Bill Gaines / Al Feldstein

subject: series
synopsis: Peyo's beloved Belgian comic chronicles the Smurfs, tiny blue forest-dwellers living in mushroom houses under Papa Smurf, forever outwitting the bumbling sorcerer Gargamel. A whimsical, gently satirical all-ages classic.
author: Peyo

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2015 weekly series following the immediate aftermath of the Death of Wolverine, with characters including X-23, Sabretooth, Daken, and Lady Deathstrike fighting over Logan's adamantium-encased corpse and his mysterious final legacy. An ambitious weekly format that spread the story thin across multiple tie-in threads.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' ambitious anthology magazine publishing literary and alternative cartoonists in the late 1990s, including Chester Brown, Joe Sacco, and Adrian Tomine. A significant venue for the alt-comics generation between the end of the anthology era and the webcomic age.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Remy LeBeau's various solo series. The character works better as a supporting player; extended solo outings struggle to sustain interest despite a charismatic protagonist.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: An early Golden Age superhero comic featuring the Blue Beetle, a skilled detective and acrobat who fights crime with gadgetry.

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin Grevioux's 2007 New Warriors: depowered mutants in stolen tech armor, led by a mysterious Night Thrasher, opposing the Initiative.

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen's 2011 Journey into Mystery: the reborn child Loki schemes to save Asgard after Fear Itself, followed by Kathryn Immonen's Sif run.
author: Kieron Gillen, Rob Rodi

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Free's 1989 series from the Giffen-DeMatteis Justice League era: lighthearted escape-artist adventures with Big Barda, by DeMatteis and Doug Moench.
author: Doug Moench, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's 2019 Dawn of X X-Men: issue-by-issue explorations of Krakoa's new mutant nation, its politics and enemies, drawn largely by Leinil Francis Yu.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2014-2015 New 52 weekly depicting Darkseid's invasion and the destruction of Earth-2, leading into Convergence.

subject: series
synopsis: David Finch's 2011 New 52 Batman series primarily showcasing Finch's detailed pencil work, featuring Batman confronting supernatural threats and an enhanced Bane, criticized for late shipping but admired visually.
author: David Finch

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1970s horror anthology featuring short supernatural tales in the tradition of the pre-code horror titles, blending atmospheric storytelling with occasional adaptations of classic horror fiction. Part of Marvel's broader bronze-age horror line alongside Tomb of Darkness and similar titles, employing artists who would later define the era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Norihiro Yagi's dark fantasy follows Clare, a half-human half-demon warrior called a Claymore who hunts shape-shifting monsters known as Yoma. Celebrated for its strong female cast, escalating power system, and increasingly bleak mythology.
author: Norihiro Yagi

subject: series
synopsis: Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer: Tanjiro Kamado joins the Demon Slayer Corps to cure his sister Nezuko, turned into a demon, and avenge his family.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' hardcover series devoting each volume to a great Disney comics artist — Romano Scarpa, Giorgio Cavazzano, Daan Jippes, Paul Murry and more.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's companion reprint series to Creepy Archives, collecting Warren Publishing's Eerie horror anthology magazine (1966–1983) in high-quality hardcover volumes. Features many of the same legendary artists as Creepy — Neal Adams, Alex Toth, Frank Frazetta covers — in atmospheric tales of supernatural horror and science fiction. An invaluable preservation of Warren's golden age.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hiromu Arakawa's masterfully plotted adventure follows brothers Edward and Alphonse Elric who use alchemy to seek the Philosopher's Stone after a forbidden transmutation costs them dearly. Balances action, humor, and profound themes of sacrifice, humanity, and systemic corruption.
author: Hiromu Arakawa

subject: series
synopsis: Yuji Itadori, a high school student with superhuman strength, swallows a cursed finger and becomes the vessel of a powerful ancient demon, entering a world of Jujutsu sorcerers. Celebrated for inventive curse designs, kinetic battles, and increasing thematic ambition.
author: Gege Akutami

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's post-House of M Excalibur revival featuring Captain Britain, Dazzler, Nocturne, and Pete Wisdom defending the UK from dimensional threats. A continuation of Claremont's long history with the team, though the book struggled to find the spark of the original Excalibur and was cancelled after 24 issues.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's anthology-style Wolverine series giving different creative teams standalone Logan stories in various settings, launched by Frank Cho with a visually spectacular Savage Land arc. Later issues by Zeb Wells, Phil Jimenez, and others used the format's flexibility to explore different tones and genres without continuity constraints.
author: Frank Cho

subject: series
synopsis: Daisuke Ashihara's manga about a defense organization that fights dimensional invaders using futuristic 'trigger' weapons. Slow-building tactical battle manga that rewards patience with intricate strategic combat and a large well-differentiated cast.
author: Daisuke Ashihara

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman and George Pérez's 1985 twelve-issue maxi-series that destroyed DC's Multiverse, killed Supergirl and Barry Allen, and rebooted the line.
author: Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Hawkman's first series (1964-1968), Gardner Fox and Murphy Anderson's Silver Age Thanagarian police couple; our files also hold Geoff Johns' 2002 run.

subject: series
synopsis: Murewa Ayodele and Lucas Werneck's 2024 Storm: Ororo Munroe as a planetary-scale hero after Krakoa.

subject: series
synopsis: Renae De Liz's digital-first origin retelling is one of the finest Wonder Woman stories ever told — warm, mythologically rich, and emotionally resonant.
author: Renae De Liz

subject: series
synopsis: J.M. DeMatteis and Ryan Sook's 2001 Spectre, with Hal Jordan as the Spirit of Vengeance seeking redemption; our files also hold Ostrander's run.
author: J M DeMatteis, John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Leah Williams' 2024 four-issue Gotham City Sirens reunion of Harley Quinn, Poison Ivy and Catwoman; files also hold Paul Dini's 2009 series.

subject: series
synopsis: Jackson Lanzing, Collin Kelly and Roger Cruz's 2024 Outsiders: Luke Fox, Kate Kane and Drummer explore the DC multiverse's hidden history, a Planetary homage.

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's second year of the Injustice prequel: Superman's regime tightens its grip as the Green Lantern Corps arrive to confront him.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's beloved fantasy series following Amy Winston, an ordinary teenager who discovers she is Amethyst, princess of the magical Gemworld. Created by Dan Mishkin, Gary Cohn, and Ernie Colón in 1983, the series blended high fantasy with superhero adventure and a coming-of-age narrative, spawning multiple acclaimed revivals across the decades.
author: Dan Mishkin, Gary Cohn

subject: series
synopsis: J.H. Williams III and W. Haden Blackman's New 52 Batwoman: Kate Kane battles the drowning ghost La Llorona and Medusa in Williams' dazzling layouts.
author: J.H. Williams III, W. Haden Blackman

subject: series
synopsis: Tomonori Inoue's manga set 20 years after a nuclear meltdown transforms Tokyo into a lethal wasteland; three genetically engineered high school girls, immune to radiation, are dispatched into the dead city to find survivors and unravel its secrets. A visually striking sci-fi thriller that uses its post-apocalyptic premise to explore themes of responsibility, sacrifice, and what it means to be human.
author: Tomonori Inoue

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Wilson carries the Captain America shield, navigating a divided America where his progressive politics make him a lightning rod. Nick Spencer's politically charged run interrogates what the Captain America symbol means for a Black man and whether patriotism and protest are compatible.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's 2008 series written by Tim Truman, faithfully adapting Robert E. Howard's Conan stories with a grittier tone and serious attention to Howard's original texts. Giorello's muscular, atmospheric linework captures the brutality and grandeur of the Hyborian Age.
author: Tim Truman

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and various artists present an extreme horror series in which a pandemic transforms victims into sadistic murderers; relentlessly brutal and divisive, it has attracted major talent including Si Spurrier and David Lapham.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Evanier and Dan Spiegle's clever action-comedy series for Eclipse Comics about Jay Endicott, a Hollywood stunt coordinator who secretly operates as the costumed vigilante Crossfire. Known for its self-aware humor, sharp dialogue, and a memorable three-issue arc that lovingly satirized comics conventions and reader expectations.
author: Mark Evanier

subject: series
synopsis: The continuation of Dragon Ball escalating into universe-threatening battles between increasingly powerful warriors. Less playful than its predecessor but enormously influential in codifying the power-scaling battle shonen genre.
author: Akira Toriyama

subject: series
synopsis: Jay Faerber and Mahmud Asrar's 2007 Image series: after the philandering hero Captain Dynamo dies, his widow recruits five of his secret children, each with one of his powers.

subject: series
synopsis: Buronson and Tetsuo Hara's post-apocalyptic martial arts epic about Kenshiro, master of a deadly pressure-point fighting style, wandering a wasteland torn apart by warlords. Extremely violent, melodramatic, and hugely influential on action manga and anime.
author: Buronson

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman and Cory Walker / Ryan Ottley's superhero epic following Mark Grayson, son of the world's greatest hero Omni-Man, who develops powers of his own — and discovers the horrifying truth about his father's origins and mission on Earth. Redefined superhero comics for a generation.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1982-1993 line of oversized prestige graphic novels: The Death of Captain Marvel, God Loves Man Kills and the New Mutants' debut among them.
author: Jim Starlin, Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's premium hardcover reprints of the early Stan Lee/Jack Kirby and Lee/Don Heck Avengers issues, collecting Earth's Mightiest Heroes in their foundational silver-age adventures. The characterization of individual Avengers established here persists in the films today.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's premium hardcover reprint series collecting the classic Stan Lee and Jack Kirby Fantastic Four issues — the foundational run that created Marvel's publishing identity in the early 1960s. Kirby's imagination was unlimited and Lee's character dynamics were electric; these volumes preserve the issues that invented Marvel's style of superhero storytelling.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: The definitive archival reprint series collecting Stan Lee and Steve Ditko's foundational Amazing Spider-Man issues, representing the origin and first classic run of one of comics' most important characters.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Frank Cho's Avengers title launched post-Civil War, featuring Tony Stark's government-sanctioned team — Ms. Marvel, Ares, Sentry, Black Widow, and others — navigating the Initiative era through Secret Invasion. A dense event-tie-in series distinguished by Cho's lush figure work.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Nunzio DeFilippis and Christina Weir's 2003 New Mutants: Dani Moonstar mentors new students at the Xavier Institute, soon relaunched as New X-Men: Academy X.
author: Christina Weir, Nunzio DeFilippis

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Schulz's strip is one of the most beloved and quietly heartbreaking works in comics. Charlie Brown's existential melancholy, Snoopy's fantasy life, and the gang's philosophical exchanges are deceptively profound.
author: Charles Schulz

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Butch Guice's Victorian-era detective series for CrossGen Comics, following the brilliant but arrogant detective Simon Archard and his mysterious partner Emma Bishop in a gaslit alternate 19th-century world where magic is real. One of CrossGen's most acclaimed titles — sharp writing, beautiful period-detailed art, and a rare genre comic with a strong female co-lead at its center.

subject: series
synopsis: The definitive collected edition of Rob Schrab's cult indie hit about a vending machine robot assassin who must keep his target alive or self-destruct, blending absurdist humor with genuine heart.
author: Rob Schrab

subject: series
synopsis: Cavan Scott's 2024 third volume of Marvel's Star Wars: The High Republic: Jedi of the golden age face the Nihil in the era's final phase.

subject: series
synopsis: Christos Gage and Doug Mahnke's 2007 Stormwatch: Post Human Division: street-level super-cops in New York policing superhumans under Jackson King.

subject: series
synopsis: Alejandro Jodorowsky and Juan Gimenez's sci-fi epic narrated by the robot Lothar chronicling the brutal, tragic dynasty of the Metabarons — the greatest warrior clan in the universe — in stories of devastating sacrifice and violent cosmic scale.
author: Alejandro Jodorowsky

subject: series
synopsis: DC's lavish 1985-1987 encyclopedic reference series covering the entire DC Universe with entries by major artists and writers, an invaluable historical document of the pre-Crisis universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Van Lente's all-ages series set in the early years of Kitty Pryde and Wolverine's mentor-student relationship at the Xavier School. Warm, witty, and accessible; a great entry point for younger readers.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Archie Comics' digest format anthology collecting classic and contemporary Archie stories in a dense, economical format. A reliable product for fans of Riverdale's classic characters.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Van Hamme and William Vance's gripping Franco-Belgian political thriller about an amnesiac man who may have been involved in a presidential assassination; consistently suspenseful with Vance's realistic, detailed art and a Bourne Identity-style conspiracy plot.
author: Jean Van Hamme

subject: series
synopsis: Suzuhito Yasuda's supernatural action manga follows a team of human and supernatural protectors guarding a town where humans and youkai coexist. Known for its stylish character designs and fun ensemble dynamic, though it took time to find its footing.
author: Suzuhito Yasuda

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Parker's series revisiting the original five X-Men in their early days at the Xavier School, with a charming Silver Age sensibility and focus on the team dynamics between Cyclops, Marvel Girl, Beast, Iceman, and Angel before the New X-Men era.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Mariko Tamaki's 2024 DC Black Label Zatanna series following the stage magician and DC's premier spellcaster through a mystery rooted in her world of showbiz and genuine supernatural power. Tamaki's character-driven approach found the melancholy beneath Zatanna's glamorous stage persona.
author: Mariko Tamaki

subject: series
synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan's 2003 Mystique: Raven Darkholme coerced into spy missions for Professor X, continued by Sean McKeever.
author: Brian K. Vaughan

subject: series
synopsis: Seminal vampire horror epic collection.
author: Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' complete hardcover reprinting of Carl Barks's Donald Duck and Uncle Scrooge comics, the gold standard of humor-adventure.
author: Carl Barks

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar's 2009 Ultimate Avengers: Nick Fury's black-ops team in three six-issue arcs with Carlos Pacheco, Leinil Yu and Steve Dillon.

subject: series
synopsis: Stuart Kerr and Vince Locke's 1986 black-and-white zombie horror: King Zombie leads the undead across a dying world as survivors flee.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell and R.B. Silva's New 52 Superboy: Kon-El as a clone grown by N.O.W.H.E.R.E., later tied to The Culling and H'el on Earth.
author: Scott Lobdell, Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's Lone Ranger: Brett Matthews and Sergio Cariello's gritty, cinematic reboot of the masked lawman and Tonto.

subject: series
synopsis: Modern X-Men run emphasizing character depth and ideological conflict.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: The fourth year of the Injustice prequel: the Olympian gods enter the war between Superman's regime and Batman's insurgency.

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's third Injustice year: John Constantine and DC's magic users join the fight against Superman's regime.

subject: series
synopsis: Marjorie Liu's 2010 X-23: Laura Kinney searches for an identity apart from Wolverine, with Sana Takeda and Phil Noto's art.
author: Marjorie Liu

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's Hellblazer (1988-2013): John Constantine's 300-issue run through Delano, Ennis, Ellis, Azzarello, Carey and Milligan.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's corporate spin-off starring a new X-Factor team — all mutants employed by Serval Industries — with a lighter tone than David's classic run, exploring what corporate-sponsored superheroes look like.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder's 2016 anthology-style Batman series featuring multiple artists exploring different aspects of Batman's rogues gallery.
author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's series bringing back Nightcrawler from the dead. The first arc is delightfully swashbuckling; subsequent arcs are more variable.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Edgar P. Jacobs's classic Belgian adventure series featuring British scientist Professor Mortimer and his friend Captain Blake in spectacular science-fiction and espionage plots; in the Tintin tradition but more SF-oriented, with a stiff upper lip and pulp imagination.
author: Edgar P. Jacobs

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 Blood Hunt tie-in series following various Marvel heroes dealing with the vampire invasion storyline across different corners of the Marvel universe. A solid event satellite series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Epic Comics' horror series expanding on the mythology of Clive Barker's Nightbreed film and his novella Cabal, following the monster community of Midian as they struggle to survive human fear and violence. The series developed storylines and characters beyond what the film depicted, though inconsistent creative teams limited its overall impact.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Van Lente's Dark Horse Comics series continuing Conan's adventures during a period of mercenary wandering across the Hyborian Age, set after his time in Cimmeria. A solid entry in the lengthy Dark Horse Conan run, later reprinted by Marvel after they reacquired the comics license in 2018.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Evanier and Will Meugniot's superhero series for Eclipse Comics featuring a team of genetically engineered artificial humans — each with different powers — who struggle for freedom and identity after being created by the Matrix Corporation. A thoughtful, character-driven book that explored questions of personhood and corporate exploitation decades before they became common themes.
author: Mark Evanier

subject: series
synopsis: The series following Wolverine's son Daken — ruthless, bisexual, manipulative — as a villain operating in a world where he wears the Dark Wolverine costume under Norman Osborn. A sharp character study of a man defined by his father's shadow.
author: Daniel Way, Marjorie Liu

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 tie-in series capitalizing on the Deadpool & Wolverine film, pitting the two anti-heroes against global threats that require their particular brand of excessive violence and irreverent banter. Delivered exactly the crowd-pleasing irreverence the film's audience expected in comics form.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tohru Fujisawa's delinquent-turned-teacher Eikichi Onizuka handles a class of problem students through unconventional methods rooted in his own rough background. A funny, surprisingly touching manga about what education and human connection can actually accomplish.
author: Tohru Fujisawa

subject: series
synopsis: A Spawn Universe series following a Wild West-era Hellspawn resurrected in the modern day, blending Western genre tropes with the supernatural mythology of the Spawn universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Peyer's 1999 series about Hourman, a time-traveling android from the future who can manipulate time, with clever time-travel storytelling and an endearingly offbeat hero trying to understand humanity.
author: Tom Peyer

subject: series
synopsis: Dylan Horrocks' Vertigo series continuing the story of Timothy Hunter from Books of Magic as a young man navigating a world reshaped by a magical revolution, struggling to master his vast potential while grappling with identity and consequence. Horrocks brought a literary, character-focused sensibility to the DC magical universe, though the series was cancelled after 25 issues.
author: Dylan Horrocks

subject: series
synopsis: Christos Gage's DC Digital First series set in the Batman Beyond future timeline, reimagining a new Justice League operating alongside the young Terry McGinnis Batman. Respectful of animated continuity and the broader DC universe, with new members and threats appropriate to the futuristic Neo-Gotham setting.
author: Christos Gage

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2024 series following General Zod and his family on a distant alien world as he attempts to build a new Kryptonian civilization unbound from his history with Superman. Joe Casey's character study explores what drives Zod beyond his hatred of the El family, finding surprising depth in a villain usually defined by theatrical menace.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: Boom! Studios' adaptation of Steve Jackson Games' wildly popular Munchkin card game, translating its dungeon-crawling parody humor — backstabbing allies, pun-laden monsters, rules-lawyering treasure hunters — into comics format with rotating creative teams. Delivers exactly the in-joke-laden humor the game's fans expect.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tomoko Ninomiya's manga about a quirky, brilliant piano student and her strict, ambitious classmate at a prestigious music conservatory in Tokyo. A warm, funny character comedy that also conveys genuine passion for classical music.
author: Tomoko Ninomiya

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Drake strikes out on his own as Red Robin following his falling-out with the new Batman, trying to prove that Bruce Wayne is still alive. A smart, character-driven series that gave Tim Drake long-overdue development.
author: Christopher Yost

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Willingham's 2006 series following a team of DC's supernatural heroes—Nightshade, Blue Devil, Ragman, Detective Chimp—as a magical strike force, spun out of Day of Vengeance.
author: Bill Willingham

subject: series
synopsis: Atsushi Ohkubo's stylish shonen action series set at the Death Weapon Meister Academy follows teams of meisters and their human-weapon partners hunting evil souls in a world of dark fantasy. Known for its distinctive pop-goth aesthetic and inventive weapon transformation system.
author: Atsushi Ohkubo

subject: series
synopsis: DC's long-running series featuring Superman's cub reporter friend Jimmy Olsen, known for bizarre transformation gimmicks and wild sci-fi premises each issue. The series reached its creative peak in 1970–1972 under Jack Kirby, who used it to introduce the Fourth World mythology — Darkseid, the New Gods, and the Forever People — permanently changing DC's cosmology.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King's 2023 DC series giving Oswald Cobblepot his most psychologically rich solo treatment — exploring the villain's family life, his complex relationship with Gotham's criminal underworld, and his deep need for respect and belonging. King's character-driven approach finds tragedy and dark humor in one of Batman's most theatrical rogues.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: John Whalen's 2007 Vertigo horror series spinning out of Swamp Thing's mythology, following the Un-Men — the monstrous creations of the mad scientist Anton Arcane — trying to build lives in a world that fears them. A compelling outsider-horror premise let down by the series' cancellation before its story fully resolved.
author: John Whalen

subject: series
synopsis: The long-running anthology collecting Scrooge McDuck's treasure-hunting adventures as written and drawn by Carl Barks, Don Rosa, and international contributors — some of the finest all-ages adventure storytelling in the medium.
author: Carl Barks

subject: series
synopsis: Pierre Christin and Jean-Claude Mézières' visionary Franco-Belgian sci-fi series following spatio-temporal agents Valérian and Laureline across time and space. Hugely influential on science fiction visual design; a direct inspiration for Star Wars and countless other SF properties.
author: Pierre Christin

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 symbiote-focused crossover event expanding the Venomverse concept with new symbiote hosts and variations, primarily appealing to dedicated Venom and symbiote readers.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Wonder Woman volume 3 (2006-2011): Allan Heinberg's relaunch, then Gail Simone's acclaimed run and J. Michael Straczynski's Odyssey, through #600.

subject: series
synopsis: Walt and Louise Simonson's comic adaptation of Blizzard's massively popular MMORPG, following an amnesiac warrior entangled in the Alliance-Horde conflict. Professional storytelling at a difficult adaptation challenge, appealing mainly to fans of the game's lore.
author: Walt Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series set in the From the Ashes X-Men era, featuring post-Krakoa mutant stories in vertical digital format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's passion project filling in untold stories from the gap between X-Men #66 and Giant-Size X-Men #1, lovingly rendered in a classic Bronze Age style for fans of the original team.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David and Todd Nauck's 1998 Young Justice: Robin, Superboy and Impulse lead a team of teen heroes in a funny, heartfelt run.
author: Peter David, Lary Stucker

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Wilson's long-running American newspaper strip and greeting card character featuring a lovable, round, hapless little fellow facing everyday misfortunes with naive optimism. A mainstay of American popular culture since the early 1970s, better known from greeting cards and merchandise than from collected strips, though his gentle philosophy of resilience has found consistent readers.
author: Tom Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: X-Men annuals from various eras. The Claremont/Cockrum annuals introducing the Badoon and others are memorable; the rotating creative teams produce variable quality.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ian Brill and James Silvani's 2010 Boom! continuation of the Darkwing Duck cartoon, opening with 'The Duck Knight Returns'.
author: Bobbi J.G. Weiss

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Tom Mandrake's 1998 ongoing solo series delving into J'onn J'onzz's multiple secret identities, his Martian history, and his status as Earth's greatest protector—a deeply sympathetic portrayal.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens' 1996 Teen Titans: the de-aged Atom leads new teen heroes Argent, Risk, Joto and Prysm.
author: Dan Jurgens

subject: series
synopsis: James Rhodes in Iron Man's armor. The original 90s series is reliable action; Pak's later 2009 series is grimly militaristic and surprisingly brutal.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Donny Cates' bombastic Thor run beginning with the Devourer King arc, where Thor must become the All-Father and face cosmic threats including a rampaging Galactus, the Black Winter, and the revelation of Beta Ray Bill's fate.
author: Donny Cates

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's 2004 Marvel Team-Up: guest-heavy team-ups building to the villain Titannus and the Golden Child arc.

subject: series
synopsis: Kyle Higgins and Eddy Barrows' New 52 Nightwing: Dick Grayson back in Gotham, haunted by the Court of Owls and his circus past, later in Chicago.
author: Kyle Higgins

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1988 Doc Savage ongoing, Denny O'Neil and Mike W. Barr's continuation of the pulp Man of Bronze and his crew.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike W. Barr's 1993 Outsiders revival with Paul Pelletier: Geo-Force's team in a darker 90s tone, with Looker turned vampire.

subject: series
synopsis: Duane Swierczynski and Eric Nguyen's 2013 Dark Horse revival of X, the brutal masked vigilante of Arcadia.

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the Brave and the Bold animated series. Team-up format with humor and heart; better than most animated tie-ins.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's digest-format anthology series reprinting classic stories from across the DC universe — Superman, Batman, Flash, Justice League, and others — in a convenient small format. A valuable archiving effort that made decades of DC history available at low cost during the late Bronze Age.
author: Various
